standard_prerequisites.name: The backward heat equation in measure form (eq: heatmeasure)
standard_prerequisites.statement: A smooth one-parameter family of probability measures (mu_t) under generalized Ricci flow satisfies the backward heat flow when d_t mu = -Delta mu.
standard_prerequisites.use: Cited at statement line 399: the two solutions mu^1_t, mu^2_t of the backward heat equation are taken in this measure form; declared as a navigation stub carrying the article's printed number.

standard_prerequisites.name: The epsilon-near-geodesic characterization of the Wasserstein distance (thm: existence)
standard_prerequisites.statement: For any two probability measures and any eps > 0 there exists a curve mu from mu^1 to mu^2 whose Lagrangian energy satisfies E(mu) <= 1/2 W_t(mu^1, mu^2)^2 + eps.
standard_prerequisites.use: Invoked at proof line 402 to choose the epsilon-near-optimal curve connecting mu^1_{t0} and mu^2_{t0}; declared as a navigation stub carrying the article's printed number.

standard_prerequisites.name: The backward-heat-equation lemma in density form (l:rhoBHE, printed 3.5)
standard_prerequisites.statement: A family mu_t = rho_t e^{-f_t} dV_t satisfies the backward heat flow in measure form if and only if the density solves d_t rho = -Delta_f rho + R^{H,f} rho.
standard_prerequisites.use: Cited at proof line 409 (together with Proposition prop: energy) when the two-parameter density families are used to bound the time-t Wasserstein distance; declared as a navigation stub.

standard_prerequisites.name: Energy monotonicity along the backward heat flow (prop: energy)
standard_prerequisites.statement: Along a backward heat flow the Lagrangian energy is nonincreasing in time: E(mu_t) <= E(mu_{t0}) for t <= t0.
standard_prerequisites.use: Invoked at proof line 409 to bound E(mu_t) by E(mu_{t0}) in the middle of the final display; declared as a navigation stub.

core_obligations: Choose an epsilon-near-optimal coupling (proof lines 402-406): by the existence theorem pick a curve mu from mu^1_{t0} to mu^2_{t0} with E(mu) <= 1/2 W_{t0}(mu^1_{t0}, mu^2_{t0})^2 + eps, where E(mu) is the Lagrangian energy of the curve at time t0.

Run the backward heat flow and bound the time-t distance (proof lines 407-409): for t <= t0 let mu_t(s) be the backward heat flow with mu_{t0}(s) = mu(s), which defines two-parameter density families (rho(s,t), phi(s,t)); by Proposition prop: energy and Lemma l:rhoBHE, 1/2 W_t(mu^1_t, mu^2_t)^2 <= E(mu_t) <= E(mu_{t0}) <= 1/2 W_{t0}(mu^1_{t0}, mu^2_{t0})^2 + eps.

Release epsilon (proof line 411): since eps > 0 is arbitrary, W_t(mu^1_t, mu^2_t) >= W_{t0}(mu^1_{t0}, mu^2_{t0}) for t <= t0, i.e. the Wasserstein distance of the two backward heat flows is nondecreasing in t.
proof_roadmap: Pick the epsilon-near-geodesic coupling at time t0 (proof lines 402-406).
Propagate along the backward heat flow and chain the energy bounds (proof lines 407-409).
Release epsilon to conclude monotonicity (proof line 411).
